statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL states that versions before 18 are not affected by CVE-2026-14676 (pg_stat_statements heap buffer overflow via crafted queries containing array constants): https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14676/ lists only major version 18. The fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/8a31ffc2d4cc5e2f3fb42b6a41b7db802716615d, corrects the normalized-query buffer size for squashed constant lists, code introduced by commit 62d712ecfd940f60e68bde5b6972b6859937c412 ("Introduce squashing of constant lists in query jumbling"), which is in PostgreSQL 18 and not on the REL_17_STABLE branch; the fix was back-patched to 18 only. pg_stat_statements.so is shipped in postgresql17-contrib, but every published DHI postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) is PostgreSQL 17, as its postgres server binary reports on both x86_64 and aarch64, so it does not contain the list-squashing code. Alpine lists this CVE under the postgresql17 17.11-r0 secfixes, but PostgreSQL 17.11 made no change for it.
